Question: how much is a building permit fee?
Bot reply:
Building permit fees follow the fee schedule of the National Building Code (PD 1096, Revised IRR), so the amount depends on your plans — mainly the use of the building, its floor area, cost and height. The Municipal Engineering Office computes the exact total.

Building fee for a single-family house, per sq. meter of floor area (the whole area is charged at its bracket's rate):
• New construction up to 20 m²: ₱2.00
• Addition/renovation up to 20 m²: ₱2.40
• Above 20 to 50 m²: ₱3.40
• Above 50 to 100 m²: ₱4.80
• Above 100 to 150 m²: ₱6.00
• Above 150 m²: ₱7.20
Example: a 75 m² house pays 75 × ₱4.80 = ₱360.

Other fees are added, for example:
• Line and grade: ₱24.00 for the first 10 m of frontage, plus ₱2.40 per extra meter
• Electrical: ₱200 for a connected load of 5 kVA or less
• Fence of masonry or concrete up to 1.80 m tall: ₱3.00 per meter
• Certificate of Occupancy: ₱100 to ₱800 depending on the computed cost (₱400 for a 75 m² house)
Plumbing and other fees depend on the fixtures and systems in your plans.

Question: how to pay real property tax?
Bot reply:
Real property tax (amilyar) is paid at the Municipal Treasurer's Office at the Municipal Hall. Bring your tax declaration or last official receipt.
• When: in full on or before March 31, or in four quarterly installments due March 31, June 30, September 30 and December 31 (Local Government Code, Sec. 250).
• How much: a percentage of your property's assessed value — the basic tax (up to 1%) plus 1% for the Special Education Fund. The Treasurer's Office computes it from your tax declaration.
• Discount: the LGU may grant up to 20% for advance or prompt payment by ordinance (Sec. 251) — ask what applies this year.
• Late payment: interest of 2% a month on the unpaid tax, up to 36 months (Sec. 255).
